approach: Add an optional `[job_plan] thrash_effort` key (default xhigh) as a small Copy enum so `JobPlanConfig` stays `Copy`. In `planning_round` (`crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs:140-155`), after `agent_spec` builds the planner spec, set `spec.effort` to the thrash effort when `round > 1 || mechanical_passes > 0`. That is the same override-after-`agent_spec` pattern as `producer.rs:339-341`. The first attempt of round 1 is untouched, and so is the critic spec built in `critic_round`. `invoke_and_record` writes `spec.effort` into the invocation record (`invocation.rs:202`), so the tests read the recorded effort back through `Records::load`. The config tests, `athena.toml`, the design doc, a new D178 and the changelog follow. `reading.rs` stays unchanged: `agent_spec` (`reading.rs:443`) already supplies the base effort and the override lives at the call site. The reading lists it as a deliverable, but no edit is needed.

decisions.choice: Store `thrash_effort` as a Copy enum `EffortLevel` (low, medium, high, xhigh, max; serde lowercase) in config.rs, with `as_str()`. `JobPlanConfig::default()` and the serde default both give `Xhigh`.
decisions.reason: `JobPlanConfig` derives `Copy` (config.rs:210) and callers move it out of `Option` with `.expect(...)`, for example `planning.rs:34-38` and `planning.rs:95-98`. A `String` field would break `Copy` and every such caller. An enum keeps them untouched and refuses an unknown value when the config is parsed.

rejected.option: A `String` field checked against `EFFORT_LEVELS` in `validate()`, like `[models]` efforts
rejected.why: It removes `Copy` from `JobPlanConfig`. That forces edits at about 50 uses across athena-core, athena-cli tests and hestia.
serde cannot deserialize into a `&'static str` from config text.

decisions.choice: Escalate in `planning_round` after `agent_spec`, by overriding `spec.effort` when `round > 1 || mechanical_passes > 0`.
decisions.reason: Both triggers are already in `Attempt` (planning.rs:89-93). The producer already overrides effort this way (producer.rs:339). One condition covers both the critic-revise and the mechanical re-plan cases, and `effort_for` stays untouched for the critic and the first call.

rejected.option: Change `agent_spec` or `Config::effort_for` to take a thrash flag
rejected.why: They are shared by every role and caller. The flag would reach roles it must not touch, such as the critic.
The verifier's model may not produce, so there is no stronger allowed model (out of scope).

decisions.choice: A kept plan seeded from an earlier job (`resumed_from`, planning.rs:48) is not treated as thrash. Its first attempt runs at the configured effort.
decisions.reason: Thrash is planner repeats within this job. The seeded first call is the first call of this job, and the reading says the first call is unchanged.

rejected.option: Treat any seeded revision as thrash
rejected.why: It widens the trigger beyond the accepted reading and costs jobs that have not thrashed.

files.purpose: Add the `EffortLevel` enum and `JobPlanConfig::thrash_effort` (serde default Xhigh, also in `Default`), plus unit tests for the default, an explicit value, the refusal of an unknown value, and the repository config.
Make the planner spec mutable and set `spec.effort` to the thrash effort when `round > 1 || mechanical_passes > 0`; document it on `plan_round`.
Add the helper `run_planned_efforts` and three tests: a critic revise, a mechanical re-plan, and a one-pass accept.
Governance file listed in the reading. Add `thrash_effort = "xhigh"` under `[job_plan]` with a comment saying which events trigger it.
Describe the escalation under the planning loop (section 3, Rounds and cost).
Append D178 with a Provenance bullet; edit no existing entry.
Add an Unreleased / Added bullet for the escalation and its key.

Add `thrash_effort: EffortLevel` to `JobPlanConfig` with `#[serde(default = "JobPlanConfig::default_thrash_effort")]` (returns `Xhigh`), and set it in `Default` (config.rs:253-264).

Do not edit earlier entries.

risks.risk: A planner call at xhigh costs more and may reach `planner_usd` ($3.00 in athena.toml:212) or the 600 s timeout, which would stop planning and make thrash worse.
risks.mitigation: The caps and timeouts are unchanged and per call (out of scope), and the preflight reserve check still runs before each call (planning.rs:113). D178 names this as the tradeoff. Whether xhigh calls hit the cap is not measured here.

risks.risk: An unknown `thrash_effort` fails as a TOML parse error, not as `ConfigError::Effort`, because the enum rejects it while the config is deserialized.
risks.mitigation: The message names the bad value and the allowed names. The test asserts the value appears in the error. The behavior is still a config error.

risks.risk: The producer finds the next decision number differently than D178 if another job appends first.
risks.mitigation: The producer reads the last heading in decisions.md in its snapshot (D177 at line 5115 in the base) and appends the next number.

risks.risk: Config files that already set `[job_plan]` and are copied between repositories keep working, but the default xhigh applies silently to them.
risks.mitigation: Intended by the reading (default xhigh). athena.toml sets it explicitly, and an operator can set `high` to turn escalation off.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in config.rs, next to `job_plan_defaults_are_off_and_bounded` (config.rs:1285). One parses `[job_plan]` with no key and asserts `thrash_effort == EffortLevel::Xhigh`. One parses `thrash_effort = "max"` and asserts `Max`. One parses `thrash_effort = "extreme"` and asserts `Config::parse` errs with a message naming the value. The existing `bad_job_plan_settings_are_refused_naming_the_field` table (config.rs:1326) also gets a `thrash_effort = "extreme"` row.
demonstrations.observes: The default is xhigh, an explicit value is read, and an unknown value makes `Config::parse` return an error naming it.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the field, the default test fails to compile or assert. Without the enum, `extreme` would be an unknown-field parse error that does not name the value, or would be accepted.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Config::parse` (config.rs:623) over text built with `unplanned(REPO_CONFIG)`. Both exist today (config.rs:1286). Step 1 adds the field and step 2 the tests.

demonstrations.method: Code inspection plus the behavior tests of criteria 3 to 5. In planning.rs, the planner spec in `planning_round` is made `mut`. After the `agent_spec` call, `if round > 1 || mechanical_passes > 0 { spec.effort = cfg.thrash_effort.as_str().to_string(); }`. The critic spec in `critic_round` is not changed, and a test asserts the critic record effort stays `high`.
demonstrations.observes: The diff of planning.rs shows the condition at the planner spec only. The tests show first-attempt planner records at `high`, later ones at `xhigh`, and critic records at `high`.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no condition the second planner record stays `high`, and the criterion 3 and 4 tests fail. With the condition on all attempts, the first-call record would be `xhigh` and the criterion 5 test fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Athena::plan_round` called through `Athena::go` in tests. The seam exists today (`run_planned` and `planning_script`, tests.rs:1193-1244).

demonstrations.method: New test `a_critic_revise_raises_the_next_planner_call_to_the_thrash_effort` in run/tests.rs. It uses `repo_with_planning(3)` (tests.rs:291) and drives `athena.go` through `finished_job`, with `planning_script(vec![good_plan()], vec![revising_critique(), accepting_critique()], calls)`. Afterwards it calls `Records::load(&athena.git, &athena.head().unwrap())`, as at tests.rs:1116, takes `jobs[job].invocations` for `Role::Planner` sorted by `seq`, and asserts the efforts are `["high", "xhigh"]`, plus `Role::Critic` records at `high`. A new helper `run_planned_efforts(repo, planner, critic) -> Vec<(Role, String)>` in tests.rs wraps `athena_with`, `finished_job` and the `Records::load` read.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core planner_effort && cargo test -p athena-data
demonstrations.observes: The first planner invocation record has effort `high` (the configured `verifier_effort` in athena.toml:21). The second has `xhigh`. The job lands, so the records are loaded. The `[job_plan]` text in the test repo sets no `thrash_effort`, so the default is exercised.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the escalation the second record is `high` and the assertion `["high","xhigh"]` fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Athena::go` into `plan_round`, with the fake driver and a scripted planner and critic queue injected through `athena_with(..., planning_script(...))` (tests.rs:190, 1193). The records are read back with `Records::load`. The script supplies only the plan and critique answers, not the effort. The effort is set by production code and recorded by `invoke_and_record`. Script and fixtures exist; the helper `run_planned_efforts` is added in step 5.

demonstrations.method: New test `a_mechanical_replan_raises_the_planner_effort`. It uses `repo_with_planning(3)` and `planning_script(vec![bad_plan(), good_plan()], vec![accepting_critique()], ..)` through `run_planned_efforts`. `bad_plan()` (tests.rs:1135) creates README.md, which exists, so Athena's plan rules give a major finding and a `RoundEnd::Mechanical` re-plan in round 1 with no critic call. It asserts the planner efforts are `["high", "xhigh"]`, and that the one critic record is at `high`.
demonstrations.observes: Round 1, `mechanical_passes` 0 gives `high`. Round 1, `mechanical_passes` 1 gives `xhigh`, and the job lands after the critic accepts.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the `mechanical_passes > 0` arm the re-planned call stays `high`. A condition on `round > 1` alone would also fail here, since the re-plan is still round 1.
demonstrations.seam: Same as criterion 3. `bad_plan` and `good_plan` exist today (tests.rs:1135-1142), and the mechanical path is already driven by `a_plan_that_still_breaks_a_rule_after_two_mechanical_passes_stops_without_the_critic` (tests.rs:1450). The helper is added in step 5.

demonstrations.method: New test `a_plan_accepted_in_one_pass_records_the_configured_planner_effort`. It uses `repo_with_planning(3)` and `planning_script(vec![good_plan()], vec![accepting_critique()], ..)` through `run_planned_efforts`. It asserts exactly one planner record, with effort `high`. It also asserts the planner efforts equal the configured `verifier_effort`, read from `Config` in the same repo.
demonstrations.observes: A job with no thrash has every planner record at the unchanged `high`.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the escalation fired on the first attempt (for example an unconditional override), the single planner record would read `xhigh` and the assertion would fail.
demonstrations.seam: Same as criterion 3. It exists, and the helper `run_planned_efforts` is added in step 5.
